0b5db31c-78f7-4194-814c-824348b60836.headline: The kills were there. The finish was a fucking mess.
0b5db31c-78f7-4194-814c-824348b60836.team: We took all three recorded Fangtooths and still lost seven structures while taking four. There was enough damage to threaten this game. The correction is knowing when to stop fighting and turn pressure into progress before the base falls apart.
0b5db31c-78f7-4194-814c-824348b60836.lossReflection: Give the shooters room to finish the push. Aurora and Kwang can turn onto Serath when she commits, while Phase keeps a safe pull available. If the wave or follow-up is missing, reset together instead of committing deeper.

focus.title: Call the prize, then stop
focus.action: After a won exchange, call one safe objective and when to reset. Make the team agree before someone spots another kill and gets a hard-on for the chase.

playerTestimony.note: Friends reported that Kwang was suicide bombing towers and the team was chasing kills for fun. This is reported behavior and intent, not telemetry or replay verification; no counts or timestamps were supplied.

b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.note: Reported tower dives described as suicide bombing.

24.4.call: This kill sequence went 1-5 after Kwang had already died shortly before it. That establishes costly overlapping deaths, not the local numbers at the start of a fight. With an ally unavailable, the default call should be to catch safe waves and preserve the next defense unless a clear, reachable advantage appears.

28.9.call: The 0-5 sequence was followed by the inner towers, inhibitor and Core falling. The priority at this stage is keeping wave clear and sustained damage alive. Back away from an unfinishable target and defend the route to the base; the record does not establish which player started the fight.

30.2.call: Two enemy kills landed while the Core fell in the same window. That is why the target call must include the base state: kill the threat that stops the defense, not simply the easiest hero to finish. The event log cannot show whether these particular kills could have saved the Core.

matchup: Belica ran a basic-attack carry build with mixed damage: treat her as a shooter, not a conventional mage.
Serath's undefeated jungle game made access to GRIM the other major concern.
build: The package rewards sustained firing with slows, attack-based bonuses and crit-boosted ability damage.
Tainted Rounds gives GRIM his own healing reduction against Serath and Terra.
The package does not fix losing access to safe targets.
eternal: Weald, Forage and Wind-Rider fit a carry who wants to finish low-health targets.
Natural Resistance is a draft alternative to Forage if control is the problem, trading farm income for a defensive trigger.
augment: System Restore pays healing and movement speed when Energy Shield blocks an ability, relevant against Belica's control.
It only pays on a blocked ability; keep it as defense without claiming it saved fights or covered basic attacks.
crest: Pacifier gives repositioning and a kill-reset, and the dash has a purpose against Serath and triggers Wind-Rider.
Its empowered damage needs physical damage, and GRIM's shots are magical, so don't count that bonus as automatic.
improvement: If diving pressure is ending firing time, compare a defensive crest at evolution instead of more damage.
Keep Tainted Rounds for independent anti-heal; Phase's Totem can grant it, but not at all times.
The current damage package is not proven to be the cause of this loss.

matchup: Phase faces Belica's ranged pressure and immobilize, then Serath and Terra up close later.
Valmont and Belica both reduce healing, so healing cannot replace spacing and timely rescue.
build: Marshal and Tainted Totem empower allies; Prophecy and Spectra reward Phase's own basic attacks.
Empowering GRIM is valuable even when stepping forward for personal on-hit damage is unsafe.
None of these completed items supplies armor.
eternal: Exarch, Preservation and Fervour support the on-hit support plan.
Fervour does not justify walking into Serath's reach; the question is whether Phase can safely keep her support triggers.
augment: Psychic Support restores a linked ally's mana, useful for GRIM's Assault Mode and other spell users.
Kindred Surge is a draft alternative for movement and regeneration, giving up this mana support.
crest: Tranquility heals and briefly mitigates nearby, suited to protecting the group rather than chasing.
Enemy healing reduction pressures the heal, but the brief mitigation still has a distinct purpose.
improvement: Enra's Blessing over Spectra protects an immobilized GRIM, trading personal on-hit damage for an automatic ally shield.
Galaxy Greaves is another defensive direction if Phase herself cannot survive the approach.
Neither makes an unsafe chase worth taking; pick by who needs protection and from what.

matchup: Serath brings repeated basic-attack damage, sustain and a low-health Salvation shield.
Terra can cleanse debuffs, so not every root stops her, and a low-health Serath is not already finished.
build: Magnify, Spectral Schematics, Dynamo and Elafrost pay off when control lands.
The synergy cannot be credited on every spell or against a target that was not immobilized.
eternal: Lotus, Flawless and Fragrance fit close-range spell fighting.
Immaculate is a draft alternative to Fragrance, trading close-range damage for mitigation near full health, not lasting brawl protection.
augment: Glacial Thorns makes Glacial Charge leave rooting crystals, adding control and a trigger for the immobilization items.
Keep it for approaches and disengages, without assuming every crossing enemy was rooted.
Deep Freeze widens the ultimate instead, trading route control for ultimate coverage.
crest: Tempest rewards staying near enemy heroes, matching Aurora's brawling range.
Valmont and Belica cut its healing and Serath punishes a long stay; value needs reachable targets and survival.
improvement: Keep the control package unless the actual problem is dying before it can work.
If incoming damage prevents a second spell rotation, compare a defensive slot against Spectral Schematics' extra damage.
Elafrost already gives physical armor; further defense should account for Belica's mixed build and Valmont.

matchup: Terra has sustain, health and both armors, and her ultimate cleanses, so she is not an easy tether target.
Serath's sustain and shield plus Belica and Valmont punish an extended exposed approach.
build: Magnify, Megacosm, Tainted Scepter and Orion form an extended damage plan against high-health targets like Terra.
No flat armor item, so it does not make a tower dive a safe commitment.
eternal: Knell, Frequency and Fracture suit sticking to one reachable opponent.
The bonuses need hero contact and buildup, so they are not unconditional durability against tower fire.
augment: Aura of the Heavens grants personal omnivamp and a smaller ally benefit, favoring fights close to teammates.
Belica and Valmont can apply anti-heal; it is sustain, not protection from burst or a tower.
crest: Tempest fits Kwang's brawling build with nearby damage and healing.
Extending a dive just to continue the aura exposes him to more damage.
improvement: If Kwang cannot survive the first exchange with Terra or Serath, compare a defensive item against Orion's slot.
Vainglory supplies both armors and builds in hero combat, but gives up Orion's offense.
Before a tower dive, confirm a survivable commitment instead of buying an excuse to force one.

matchup: Renna finished with little damage, but that does not prove why her impact was low.
The clearer threats came later: Serath reaching a shooter, Terra's armors, and Belica's carry build.
build: Mystic Marksman makes the sniper shot magical, giving Tainted Scepter and Wraith Leggings' penetration a coherent target.
Noxia needs a separate ability after the mark, not repeated casts of the same shot.
eternal: Lotus, Early Bloom and Immaculate suit a ranged plan that avoids the first hit.
Once poked low, Immaculate stops protecting, so it cannot cover a full Serath dive.
augment: Mystic Marksman makes Knock, Knock! magical, explaining the power and penetration choices.
Enemy magical armor, including Terra's Vainglory, matters more to the shot; keep the coherent conversion.
crest: Epoch's stasis waits out danger but gives no escape distance, so it needs a survivable position afterward.
Holding it for a dangerous Serath commitment is a defensive plan.
improvement: There is no automatic need for another offensive item.
If magical armor blunts the spell combination, compare penetration; if Serath ends the attempt first, compare protection.
Phase and GRIM also supply anti-heal, so assess coverage before treating the Tainted Scepter slot as mandatory.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Keep the damage coming from somewhere safe. When Serath disappears, hold the escape and shield for her arrival. A fleeing target is bait if reaching it leaves GRIM exposed.
After a won fight, hit the safe structure or reset with the team. Don’t let another potential kill drag the carry away from the job.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: The healing and vision were useful. Keep enabling GRIM while maintaining a safe place to pull him back toward.
Link is not a fucking suicide pact. Call the retreat before the carry gets immobilized; following the deepest diver just gives the team another person to rescue.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Strong farming, damage and our highest objective damage. Keep that contribution, then make the next commitment a clear team call.
When Serath reaches GRIM, use the root to buy him shooting time. Sometimes the winning engage is turning around, not chasing their backline farther away.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620: Stop raw-dogging towers without an exit. Confirm the wave, who can follow and how the dive ends. No plan, no dive.
Leading our damage and our deaths is a mixed review. Keep the pressure, but protect the shooters when pursuing another target would abandon the push.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac: Keep the ranged pressure and objective contribution. Use Sonar to cover the approach while the team advances.
When a target retreats beyond the safe push, let it go. Save camouflage for repositioning when Serath closes.
